page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores and 1080 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz. The machine is driven by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors featuring a 4.2 GHz clock speed and 504 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. As a bare-metal instance without hypervisor intervention, it provides full low-level access to the underlying hardware. The configuration does not include local disk storage or hardware GPUs, requiring persistent data to be handled over cloud network storage.

Benchmark evaluations place this machine in the top tier for multi-core computation and memory throughput. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 313,180.49 and a PassMark CPU score of 178,785.41. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 1,087.82 GB/sec, while write operations exceed 428 GB/sec. In memory-intensive services, the platform achieved 413.48 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 164.82 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Extended CPU instruction tests and cryptographic operations similarly placed in the top decile. However, while prompt processing on moderate language models leverages the CPU vector extensions effectively, token generation throughput without dedicated GPUs is limited.

Featuring 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, this platform provides high computational density for large-scale enterprise deployments. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external network disk solutions, which introduces an architectural latency tradeoff for I/O-intensive pipelines. The configuration is primarily suited for large in-memory databases, Redis clusters, massive parallel software builds, and heavy multi-threaded compute workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal server engineered for enterprise-scale computational workloads and dense in-memory processing. Powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors with 144 physical cores, 288 dedicated vCPUs, and a 504 MB L3 cache, the system operates at 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 1080 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, offering 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server features no bundled local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs. In multi-threaded benchmarking, the machine exhibits top-tier throughput in multi-core processing, PassMark database calculations, and Redis SET operations reaching over 413 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth scales past 1,000 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Lacking local storage, it relies on network storage solutions. This hardware profile suits high-concurrency database deployments, intensive multi-threaded software compilation, massive in-memory caching layers, and high-throughput batch compute operations.
